posts.why: Sequencing errors are the most expensive mistake in small business marketing.

tiktok.hook: They bought adverts before fixing the reply. That made it worse.
beats: So they paid to be ignored
tiktok.vo: This business bought adverts for four months before it fixed the reply, which means every week they paid to send strangers into a chat where nobody answered for two days. More reach made it worse, because more people arrived to be ignored. The leak was never at the top. It was three days downstream of the money.
tiktok.cap: The leak was not at the top. It was three days downstream of the money.
tiktok.body: Four months of adverts sending strangers into a chat nobody answered for two days. More reach made it worse — more people arrived to be ignored. The leak was downstream, not at the top.

instagram.cap:
The cheapest audit in any small business is not the advert account. It is the last twenty conversations, read in order, with the timestamps.

Fix the answer before you buy the question.

facebook.body:
A business I looked at had been buying adverts for four months before fixing the reply.

Every week they paid to send strangers into a chat where nobody answered for two days.

More reach made it worse — more people arrived to be ignored.

The leak was never at the top. It was three days downstream of the money.

Where is yours?

posts.topic: A website you do not need
posts.why: The most disarming sales position available.

tiktok.hook: We will not sell you a website you do not need.
tiktok.vo: We will not sell you a website you do not need. Sometimes the answer is that your replies are the problem. Sometimes it is one sentence on the page you already have. Sometimes it is that nobody can find you and a site would not help. Ask first, it is free, and I would rather tell you no than take four thousand naira and watch you get nothing.
tiktok.cap: Ask before you buy. Sometimes the answer is "not yet", and that is free to hear.
tiktok.body: Sometimes the answer is your replies. Sometimes it is one sentence on the page you already have. Sometimes it is that nobody can find you. Ask first, it is free.

instagram.cap:
Saying no to the wrong project protects the referral, and referrals are the only marketing a small studio actually has.

The most profitable sentence in sales is sometimes 'not yet'.

facebook.body:
We will not sell you a website you do not need.

Sometimes the answer is that your replies are the problem. Sometimes it is one sentence on the page you already have. Sometimes it is that nobody can find you, and a site would not fix that.

Ask first. It is free. I would rather tell you no than take your money and watch you get nothing.

What would you ask?

posts.why: A published policy is a permanent proof point.

tiktok.hook: Three things we always refuse: fake proof, fake urgency, fake results.
tiktok.vo: Three things we always refuse. Fake proof, meaning testimonials and logos that were not earned. Fake urgency, meaning countdowns that reset and stock levels that are not real. And fake results, meaning any promise about an outcome we do not control. Write your own three, publish them, and then you have a policy instead of a mood, which is the difference between a standard and a preference.
tiktok.cap: Fake proof. Fake urgency. Fake results. Write your three and publish them.
tiktok.body: Fake proof, fake urgency, fake results. Write your own three and publish them — that is the difference between a standard and a preference.

instagram.cap:
This works for any business. Three sentences, on the about page, and suddenly the rest of the page has something to be consistent with.

A published refusal list is a standard. An unpublished one is a mood.

facebook.body:
Three things we always refuse:

1. Fake proof — testimonials and logos that were not earned.
2. Fake urgency — countdowns that reset, stock levels that are not real.
3. Fake results — any promise about an outcome we do not control.

Write your own three and publish them. That is the difference between a standard and a preference.

What would yours be?

posts.why: Reframes restraint as a marketing skill.

tiktok.hook: The best marketing decision is usually not yet. Fix the leak first.
tiktok.vo: The best marketing decision is usually not yet, because buying attention before you can hold it is the most reliable way to waste money in this business. Fix the leak: the reply time, the first sentence, the price being visible. Then buy attention, because now attention converts. Same budget, different order, wildly different year.
tiktok.cap: Attention before a working funnel is a donation with analytics.
tiktok.body: Same budget, different order. Fix reply time, first sentence, visible price — then buy attention, because now attention converts.

instagram.cap:
This is hard advice to follow when you are impatient, which is why it is worth writing down before the impatience arrives.

A donation with analytics is still a donation.

facebook.body:
The best marketing decision is usually 'not yet'.

Buying attention before you can hold it is the most reliable way to waste money in this business.

Fix the leak first: reply time, the first sentence, a visible price. Then buy attention — because now attention converts.

Same budget. Different order. Wildly different year.

Which one are you skipping?

posts.topic: We talked someone out of a project
posts.why: The story earns the right to sell later.

tiktok.hook: We talked someone out of a project. Best work we did.
beats: The problem was they had no traffic
And no way to capture it
tiktok.vo: We talked someone out of a new website this month. Their site was fine. The problem was that nobody was arriving and nothing captured the people who did. So they spent the money on three months of local ads and a proper WhatsApp reply system instead, and they got customers. We lost a project and gained a reference, which in a market this small is the better trade.
tiktok.cap: We lost a project and gained a reference. That is the better trade here.
tiktok.body: Their site was fine. Nobody was arriving and nothing captured the people who did. They spent the money on local ads and a reply system instead. We lost the project and gained a reference.

instagram.cap:
In a small market, the person you talked out of a bad purchase tells three people. The person you sold a bad purchase also tells three people, but differently.

Turning down the wrong project is how you get the right ones.

facebook.body:
We talked someone out of a new website this month.

Their site was fine. The problem was that nobody was arriving, and nothing captured the people who did.

So they spent the money on three months of local ads and a proper WhatsApp reply system instead. They got customers.

We lost a project and gained a reference. In a market this small, that is the better trade.

posts.topic: Ask any agency what they would not do
posts.why: Gives the buyer an interview technique.

tiktok.hook: Ask any agency what they refuse to do. That is the interview.
tiktok.vo: Ask any agency or freelancer what they would refuse to do, and listen to how quickly the answer comes. If they have a list, they have standards and you can predict how the project will go. If they say nothing, they are for hire in every direction, which means your project is the first thing that will get bent when the money runs short. One question, better than a portfolio.
tiktok.cap: The refusal list is the portfolio. Everything else is decoration.
tiktok.body: A list of refusals means standards, and standards mean you can predict how a project will go. Silence means the project bends the moment money runs short.

instagram.cap:
It works for builders, tailors, caterers and agencies. The speed of the answer tells you more than the content.

Paste this question into your next supplier conversation.

facebook.body:
Ask any agency or freelancer what they would refuse to do, and listen to how quickly the answer comes.

If they have a list, they have standards, and you can predict how the project will go.

If they say nothing, they are for hire in every direction — which means your project is the first thing that gets bent when the money runs short.

One question beats a portfolio.

posts.why: A small, repeatable habit phrased as a question.

tiktok.hook: Nobody regrets asking "do I need this?" Plenty regret not asking.
tiktok.vo: Nobody has ever regretted asking do I need this before buying something. Plenty have regretted not asking, and you can hear them in the reviews. One question, ten seconds, and it works on software, on adverts, on courses, on packs, including mine, which is why I put it on my own sales page.
tiktok.cap: Ask "do I need this?" before you pay. Ten seconds, no downside.
tiktok.body: One question, ten seconds, and it works on software, adverts, courses and packs — including ours, which is why we put it on the sales page.

instagram.cap:
If the answer is 'maybe', wait a day. Most purchases survive one night of thinking and the ones that do not were never going to be used.

The question has no downside and the answer is usually clear.

facebook.body:
Nobody has ever regretted asking 'do I need this?' before buying something.

Plenty have regretted not asking — you can hear them in the reviews.

One question. Ten seconds. It works on software, adverts, courses and packs, including mine, which is why it is on my own sales page.

What did you buy without asking?

posts.topic: Has anyone told you not to buy
posts.why: Rarity is the point, and the memory is the proof.

tiktok.hook: Almost nobody has been told not to buy. Everyone remembers it.
tiktok.vo: I asked people whether a seller had ever told them not to buy something. Almost nobody had, and the few who had remembered the shop, the product, and roughly what year it was. One woman said she has been going back to that shop for nine years because of one sentence. That is what a refusal buys you: a customer who tells the story for a decade.
tiktok.cap: Almost nobody had been told not to buy. Everyone who had remembered it for years.
tiktok.body: Almost nobody had been told not to buy something, and the few who had remembered the shop, the product and roughly what year it was. One woman had been going back for nine years.

instagram.cap:
This is the strongest argument for honesty in sales that I have found, and it came from strangers on a street rather than a book.

A refusal is the only marketing that gets retold for free.

facebook.body:
I asked people whether a seller had ever told them not to buy something.

Almost nobody had. The few who had remembered the shop, the product, and roughly what year it was.

One woman said she has been going back to that shop for nine years because of one sentence.

That is what a refusal buys: a customer who tells the story for a decade.

posts.topic: Built is a project, not a pack
posts.why: Separates the two products so nobody buys the wrong one.

tiktok.hook: Built for you is a project, not a pack. Ask which.
tiktok.vo: If you want the work done for you, that is a project, not a pack. A pack is files you open, but a project is a person, a date, and a number much bigger than five thousand. I will tell you honestly whether your job is one I can do well. Some I will pass to somebody else who does that thing better, and I will say which is which.
tiktok.cap: Packs are files. Projects are people. Message PROJECT on WhatsApp 0905 069 0837 and we will say honestly.
tiktok.body: A pack is files you open. A project is a person, a date and a number much bigger than five thousand. I will tell you honestly which one your job is, and pass it on if it is not mine.

instagram.cap:
Most bad agency experiences start with a client buying a project expecting a pack, or a pack expecting a project.

Two products, two promises. Confusing them costs both of us.

facebook.body:
If you want it built for you, that is a project, not a pack.

A pack is files you open. A project is a person, a date, and a number much bigger than ₦5,000.

I will tell you honestly which one your job is — and if it is not something I do well, I will say so and point you at someone who does.

Message PROJECT on WhatsApp: 0905 069 0837.

posts.topic: The project we declined this month
posts.why: Same format as the earlier refusals, which is what makes it a series.

tiktok.hook: We declined an online shop for a business with no stock.
tiktok.vo: The project we declined this month was a full online shop for a business that did not yet have stock. A beautiful storefront with nothing behind it, six weeks of work, and the first customer would have found an empty catalogue. We suggested they sell through WhatsApp for three months first, prove people want the thing, then build. They did. They are not ready for a shop yet, and now they know.
tiktok.cap: A shop with no stock is a six week way to find out nobody could buy.
tiktok.body: A full storefront with nothing behind it, six weeks of work, and the first customer finds an empty catalogue. Sell through WhatsApp for three months first, prove demand, then build.

instagram.cap:
The cheapest ecommerce platform in Lagos is a WhatsApp catalogue and a spreadsheet. It also tells you whether anyone wants the product at all.

Prove the demand before you build the storefront.

facebook.body:
The project we declined this month was a full online shop for a business that did not yet have stock.

A beautiful storefront with nothing behind it. Six weeks of work, and the first customer would have found an empty catalogue.

We suggested selling through WhatsApp for three months first, proving people want the thing, then building.

They did. They are not ready for a shop yet — and now they know.

posts.why: A checklist that survives after the month ends.

tiktok.hook: Three questions before any marketing spend: what leaks, who owns it.
beats: If any answer is unclear, wait
tiktok.vo: Three questions before any marketing spend. What leaks, meaning where are you currently losing people. What changes if this works, meaning do you have the capacity to handle double the messages. And who owns it, meaning the domain, the account, the list. If any of the three is unclear, wait a week, because the money is easier to keep than to earn back.
tiktok.cap: What leaks · what changes · who owns it. Ask all three before you pay.
tiktok.body: Where are you losing people, can you handle double the messages, and who owns the domain, account and list. If any answer is unclear, wait a week.

instagram.cap:
The second question is the one nobody asks, and it is the one that turns a good campaign into a bad month.

Three questions that cost nothing and save everything.

facebook.body:
Three questions before any marketing spend:

1. What leaks? Where are you currently losing people?
2. What changes if this works? Can you handle double the messages?
3. Who owns it? The domain, the account, the list.

If any of the three is unclear, wait a week. The money is easier to keep than to earn back.

Which one would you fail today?
